title: Bootstrap & Upgrade Failure Playbook and Terraform Notes
content:
TL;DR: Practical playbook for common bootstrap/install and upgrade failures for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). Includes quick triage checklist, Terraform module pitfalls, and an upgrade plan with rollback and smoke tests. This is a working draft — use for runbooks and embed into runbook-runner later.

Scope:
- Applies to Private (VPC) and on-prem packaged installs managed by our Terraform modules and Kubernetes startup charts.
- Covers: network and DNS, certs, container runtime & drivers, model weight downloads, persistent storage mounts, worker/node failures, and runtime incompatibilities triggered by upgrades.
- Excludes onboarding sales/procurement steps.

Before you run anything (quick pre-flight)
- Confirm access: can you reach customer VPC jump host and k8s API? (ssh / kubectl)
- Check terraform state access: S3/GCS bucket + lock (dynamo/filestore) available.
- Note current versions: terraform --version, kubectl version, helm version, redwood-operator image tag, runtime image tag.

Commands to keep handy:
- kubectl get pods -A -o wide
- kubectl logs -n redwood <pod> --since=10m
- kubectl describe pod -n redwood <pod>
- journalctl -u containerd -n 200 --no-pager
- sudo systemctl status nvidia-driver.service (on GPU nodes)
- terraform plan -var-file=customer.tfvars
- terraform apply -parallelism=10 -auto-approve (only in CI or with approval)

Quick triage checklist (3-minute)
- Can k8s API respond? kubectl get nodes; if not, check kube-apiserver logs on control plane.
- DNS resolution inside cluster? kubectl run --rm -i --tty dnscheck --image=busybox -- nslookup google.com
- Disk pressure / OOM kills: kubectl get nodes -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.conditions[?(@.type=="MemoryPressure")].status}'
- Image pull failures: describe pod to see ImagePullBackOff / ErrImagePull and check registry creds.
- Model weights failing to download: check host has outbound access to model storage and signed URL TTL.
- Certificate errors: check webhook/admission-controller logs for TLS handshake errors.

Common bootstrap failure scenarios (symptom -> quick checks -> remediation)
1) Control plane unreachable after bootstrap
   - Symptom: kube-apiserver not reachable from jump host; terraform apply reports timeout attaching LB or updating target groups.
   - Quick checks: curl <apiserver-lb-ip>:6443 from jump; check cloud provider's target group/healthchecks; kubectl not available.
   - Likely causes: wrong security group rules, healthcheck path mismatch, provider quotas, LB IP assigned in private subnet.
   - Remediation: verify security group egress/ingress rules; ensure control plane nodes in public subnet or LB in correct AZs; temporarily open port 6443 from admin IP; re-run terraform apply with correct subnet_id.

2) Nodes repeatedly NotReady or flapping
   - Symptom: kubelet registering then un-registering; NodeNotReady state.
   - Quick checks: journalctl -u kubelet, container runtime logs, check cni plugin pods.
   - Likely causes: MTU mismatch on VPC, misconfigured CNI, kernel incompatible with driver, disk pressure.
   - Remediation: confirm MTU on ENI / on-prem switch (jumphost ip link show); validate CNI DaemonSet logs (calico/ctr); if disk pressure, evict pods or increase node disk.

3) Worker GPU nodes fail to load model runtime
   - Symptom: inference pod CrashLoopBackOff; logs show CUDA init errors or /dev/nvidia not present.
   - Quick checks: lsmod | grep nvidia; nvidia-smi on node; driver version vs container toolkit version.
   - Likely causes: driver mismatch, incorrect docker runtime config, missing kernel module.
   - Remediation: reinstall drivers matching driver version pinned in terraform module, ensure containerd config has nvidia runtime or install NVIDIA container toolkit, reboot node. Document driver version in terraform variables for future upgrades.

4) Model weights fail to mount or download (large-file timeouts)
   - Symptom: pods stuck at Init with curl/gsutil timeouts; long-tail download errors during bootstrap.
   - Quick checks: curl from node to storage endpoint with same URL, check MTU/sem and proxy settings, check signed URL TTL.
   - Likely causes: large downloads throttled by NAT gateway, proxy drops, presigned URL TTLs shorter than startup time.
   - Remediation: pre-seed model weights into node-local cache or persistent PV during bootstrap; increase NAT gateway capacity or use VPC endpoint for storage; extend TTL on signed URLs; add retry logic in init container.

5) Admission webhooks / operator crash loops after upgrade
   - Symptom: deployments failing due to 500/502 from webhook; operator CrashLoopBackOff with schema migration errors.
   - Quick checks: kubectl logs operator, describe ValidatingWebhookConfiguration, check certificate expiration.
   - Likely causes: API changes between operator versions, CRD version mismatch, webhook cert rotation not completed.
   - Remediation: roll back to previous operator image, run CRD migration job in maintenance window, ensure cert-manager has resources to rotate certs.

Terraform module notes (practical gotchas)
- Provider versions: pin terraform provider versions (aws, google, kubernetes, helm) in modules/<name>/versions.tf. Unpinned providers break downstream.
- State locking: ensure dynamodb or GCS locking is configured. Mistakes here cause concurrent apply races.
- Backend perms: the CI user must have GetObject/PutObject for state bucket and PutItem on DynamoDB. Document the minimal IAM policy (keep in infra repo).
- Subnet tagging: our modules look for tag "redwood:private-subnet=true" — common customer mistake is not tagging subnets created outside module.
- MTU and CNI: modules expose mtu variable; default 1500 but many on-prem networks use 9000 — mismatches cause flapping.
- Image registry creds: module creates docker config secret only if var.registry_credentials != ""; include in tfvars for private registries.
- Immutable resource name changes: avoid changing resource names for stateful resources (e.g., EBS volumes, PVs) — track in upgrade notes.
- Module versioning: use semantic tagging and a changelog entry for any breaking default change (especially defaults for security groups or egress).

Terraform troubleshooting quick list
- terraform plan fails with diff showing replacement of PVs: inspect provider.experienced_changes = true in state and check for changed block device mapping.
- apply hangs waiting for LB to become healthy: check security groups + health check path + target registration.
- drifts: terraform refresh then plan to see drift; for PVs, sometimes external processes change tags or lifecycle rules.

Upgrade plan (template)
1) Pre-upgrade (2–3 days before)
   - Inventory: list clusters, node counts, images, operator versions, kernel and driver versions; store in upgrade ledger.
   - Smoke baseline: run standard smoke test and save traces/latency (see smoke tests below).
   - Backup: export etcd snapshot, backup any configmaps/secrets (sops or KMS encrypted), snapshot persistent volumes if feasible.
   - Dry-run in staging: apply identical terraform/helm changes in staging that mirrors production.

2) Maintenance window and canary (hour 0)
   - Apply terraform changes for infra that are non-disruptive first (security group updates, subnets).
   - Upgrade operator on dedicated canary namespace / one node pool. Validate ingress, webhooks, outbound calls.
   - Run smoke tests; if pass, gradually roll out across node pools (maxUnavailable conservative).

3) Post-upgrade validation (0–4 hours after)
   - Run full smoke test suite. Compare to baseline. Watch tracing and SLO dashboards for <10% regression.
   - Verify model outputs for a deterministic prompt set (end-to-end regression check).

4) Rollback plan (if smoke tests fail)
   - Operator or runtime issues: immediately scale down new deployment via kubectl scale and restart previous replicaSet (if using replicasets).
   - Infra-level failure: revert terraform to previous revision in state bucket (use a locked plan) and apply only the revert. If state drift, escalate to infra on-call.
   - Database/CRD migration failure: restore etcd snapshot and reapply old manifests. Document that this will roll back any metadata changes since snapshot.

Smoke test checklist (post-bootstrap / post-upgrade) — quick pass/fail
- API reachability: curl -I https://<admin-router>/healthz -> 200 within 500ms
- Small inference: POST /v1/generate with prompt "cat facts" -> token output begins within 150ms and completes (or streaming begins)
- Embeddings: /v1/embeddings responds with vectors (length matches model spec)
- Model checksum: run small validation job that loads model weights and checks expected sha256 tag
- KV cache sanity: write/read key via redis/kv endpoint, TTL set as expected
- Disk / PVs: run df -h inside inference pod; confirm PV mounts on worker nodes
- GPU health: nvidia-smi returns processes for inference pods (if GPUs used)
- Logs ingestion: new logs appear in customer log sink (test via test message and search)
- Latency smoke: 95p latency within expected range vs baseline (note absolute numbers in ledger)

Postmortem / incident notes format (copy this into any incident)
- Summary: one-line
- Impact: services affected, customer-visible impact
- Timeline: UTC timestamps for each significant event
- Root cause: short description + evidence
- Remediation: what we did now
- Action items: who owns longer-term fixes (link to Jira)

Examples of small helper scripts (snippet ideas)
- pre-seed-models.sh -> prefetch weights to /var/lib/redwood/models with retries and exponential backoff
- quick-healthcheck.sh -> runs the smoke checklist and prints summary JSON (used by CI)

Known open questions / TODOs:
- Decide TTL policy for presigned model download URLs during node bootstrap (short term we extend to 2h, long term design a private registry).
- Add terraform true/false variable to disable automatic GPU driver install (customers sometimes want manual install).
- Improve instrumentation around slow downloads (capture node-level histogram).
- Add more deterministic prompt set for regression checks (curate across models).

Appendix A — Useful links and references
- Infra repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-terraform (PRs, module docs)
- Upgrade runbook template: CONFLUENCE-12345
- Model weight storage runbook: CONFLUENCE-21999

Notes to self / rough items to clean up before finalizing
- Convert this doc into a structured runbook for the runbook-runner tool (need JSON schema).
- Add concrete terraform variable examples for common cloud providers (aws/gcp/azure).
- Add K8s manifest snippets for safe webhook rollouts.

Unresolved: how to handle customers with restrictive outbound proxies that break model downloads — proposal: pre-seed to an internal object-store via sftp during on-site installation.

End of draft - feedback welcome.
